Result: Strong-allocation MAE was 5.786 pooled versus 5.438 equal; 4/12 dominant-donor arrangements worsened. SD was a post hoc diagnostic.
Interpretation: Equal-donor averaging did not improve accuracy in every arrangement.

Design: Four panels, two solvers, 24 draws; 645,120 predictions
Result: Top100 NNLS equal-minus-pooled MAE was −0.285 points, but removing five abundant genes reversed it to +0.182. The reversal occurred in all three seed blocks. Across eight settings, conditional SD differences were +0.993 to +1.907.
Interpretation: The direction of the accuracy difference depended on gene selection.

Stage: External PBMC v3 failure and v3.1
Design: Six donors; two panels/two solvers; full v3.1 grid of 2,419,200 predictions
Result: Initial SLSQP oracle discrepancy 6.722 × 10⁻⁵ exceeded 5 × 10⁻⁵. Uniformly tightening ftol from 10⁻¹² to 10⁻¹⁴ yielded a complete passing run; scientific design and acceptance limits stayed fixed. Top100 NNLS MAE improved 0.433 points while conditional SD increased 1.694.
Interpretation: The initial failed run was retained. The pancreas gene-removal reversal was not reproduced across the four PBMC settings.

Design: Reconstructed saved v2 reference signatures; no new proportion predictions
Result: Strong-allocation equal/pooled signature-variance trace ratio was 3.466 theoretically and 3.411 empirically.
Interpretation: The signature-variance result was consistent with finite-population sampling; its contribution to variation in estimated proportions was not quantified.

Design: Same saved PBMC cell IDs; raw counts; 720 references; 86,400 predictions
Result: Weighted MAE 5.634→6.361; ordinary MAE 9.110→9.227; difference in differences +0.610 points. Weighted absolute error and conditional SD remained lower.
Interpretation: Tests donor allocation within the existing MuSiC workflow; the comparison does not identify a mechanism or a generally optimal allocation.
